content: VectorFoundations: Components, magnitude, addition and subtraction—the grammar of direction meets quantity across three connected islands
VectorOperations: Dot product, cross product, projection and reflection—measuring alignment, creating perpendiculars, decomposing motion
VectorDynamics: Vector fields, force vectors, and motion—flow, curl, divergence, velocity and acceleration as vectors
VectorAdvanced: Torque, advanced exercises, and throwing—rotational forces, attraction magnitude, physics interaction across four islands
VectorWorkbench: Universal sandbox—all vector operations computed simultaneously in one diamond arena, transition to forces
ForcesFoundations: Newton's laws, projectile motion, friction—F=ma made tangible, then become the projectile via jump pad
ForcesSystems: Attractors, force fields, springs and particles—four islands of force systems connected by jump pads in clockwise circuit
ForcesChaos: N-body dynamics and strange attractors—three-body problem, chaos, deterministic unpredictability across two islands
ForcesArena: Drone combat, destruction sandbox, and exhibition gallery—applied forces break things, then a gallery of everything learned
forces.demonstration: See vectors as arrows in space. Add them head-to-tail. Feel dot product measure alignment. Watch cross product create perpendicular vectors. Then feel gravity pull you down. Push objects and feel resistance. Watch attraction and repulsion create orbits and explosions.
forces.description: The fundamental language of 3D space meets the physics that brings it to life. Vectors encode direction and magnitude—the building blocks of everything spatial. Forces convert those vectors into motion through Newton's laws. Master vectors, master forces, master the physical world.
forces.formula: v = (x,y,z), |v| = √(x²+y²+z²), F = ma → a = F/m → v += a·dt → p += v·dt
learning_objectives: Coordinate systems and spatial reasoning in 3D
Vector components: x, y, z as decomposed direction
Addition and subtraction: combining and differencing vectors
Cross product: creating perpendicular vectors, torque, normals
Projection and reflection: mirrors and collisions
Vector fields: spatial functions mapping position to direction
F = ma: Force equals mass times acceleration
Friction and drag: resistance to motion
Attraction and repulsion: inverse square laws
Particle systems: many bodies under forces
N-body dynamics: gravitational chaos from simple rules
forces.name: Vectors & Forces: From Direction to Dynamics
forces.qfep_connection: Vectors define system states—the S in QFEP. Forces introduce change—they drive the temporal evolution φΔE(S,t). Together, vectors and forces are the complete grammar of physical motion: direction encodes where, magnitude encodes how much, and F=ma encodes why things change.
forces.truth: Direction + magnitude = vector. F = ma. Acceleration is the only thing you feel. Position and velocity are states; force is what changes them.
